purpose: Define the safety and correctness contract of the caliper-docgen `lsp` subcommand's stdin/stdout JSON-RPC framing: it never allocates an unbounded receive buffer from an untrusted Content-Length header, it never desyncs its framing on a headerless or malformed message, and it truthfully advertises hoverProvider (the one capability this spec asserts, per AC-003) matching whether a real handler exists for it.
scope: crates/cli/src/commands/lsp.rs: Content-Length header parsing and size-bounding, frame-body reading, the response to an 'initialize' request, and stream-EOF handling. Also crates/cli/src/main.rs's `Command::Lsp` match arm (`cmd_lsp()?`), solely as the mechanism by which an Err returned from lsp.rs becomes process exit code 1 — the generic Err-to-exit-1 mapping itself (which applies identically to every subcommand) is asserted once by SPEC-CLI-001a and is not re-derived here; this spec only asserts that lsp.rs returns Err for the specific conditions in AC-001 and AC-004, and verifies end-to-end exit code 1 as a black-box regression check. AC-005/AC-005b/AC-005c/AC-005d describe the current exit-0 (Ok(())) EOF/truncation paths, and AC-006/AC-007 describe the current continue-the-loop paths for malformed frame bodies — neither of these produces an Err or exit code 1. Does not cover file writes (lsp never writes a file, per SPEC-CLI-001b AC-001) or config loading (lsp accepts but ignores --config, per SPEC-CLI-001d).
non_goals: The extraction/resolution logic itself — owned by crates/core, a separate capability under a separate spec.
NAPI/Node binding entry points — owned by crates/binding, a separate capability.

Implementing a working textDocument/hover handler for the LSP command. lsp.rs is an explicit scaffold today; this spec only requires that hoverProvider is truthfully advertised as false while no handler exists, not that hover itself works.

Implementing or asserting any LSP method dispatch beyond the initialize response. shutdown and exit dispatch exist in lsp.rs today (shutdown replies with a null-result response frame; exit breaks the read loop and returns Ok(())) but are not asserted by any criterion in this spec — no other request or notification handlers are in scope either.

The specific 16 MiB size threshold's tunability (e.g. via a flag or config field) — the threshold is a fixed constant in lsp.rs; changing it to be configurable is a separate feature, not part of this safety contract.

Distinguishing a truncated/malformed connection close (AC-005b, AC-005c, AC-005d) from a clean zero-byte EOF (AC-005) with a distinct exit code or logged error. Currently read_content_length's Err(()) return (covering clean EOF, a truncated header block, and non-UTF-8 header bytes alike, since reader.read_line(...).unwrap_or(0) == 0 maps any io::Error to the same 0-bytes-read outcome as a real EOF) and cmd_lsp's read_exact(...).is_err() branch (covering a truncated body) both collapse into the same exit-0, no-response-frame outcome as a clean disconnect. lsp.rs's own doc comment on read_content_length ('Err(()) means the stream ended before any header line was read at all') is inaccurate for this reason — it also fires on a partial or malformed header. Changing this to return a distinguishing enum (e.g. {CleanEof, PartialHeader, PartialBody}) and exiting non-zero for the non-clean-EOF cases is a follow-up implementation decision, not required by this spec, which documents the current behavior as-is.

Recovering or logging anything for a frame with a valid, in-range Content-Length whose body is not parsable JSON, or whose parsed JSON has no string 'method' member (AC-006, AC-007) beyond continuing the read loop — no diagnostic or stderr message is emitted for either case today.

The truthfulness of the initialize response's textDocumentSync capability (currently advertised as 1, i.e. full-document sync) against the fact that no textDocument/didOpen, didChange, or didClose handler exists in cmd_lsp's dispatch (all three fall through the `_ => {}` arm). This spec's truthful-advertisement requirement applies only to hoverProvider (AC-003) since that is the capability REQ-CLI-001 names as its example; textDocumentSync: 1 is advertised today with no sync handler behind it, and reconciling that mismatch — either by implementing sync handlers or by changing the advertised value — is separate work not asserted by any criterion here.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: An LSP client sending a Content-Length header declaring a value greater than 16 MiB (16777216) causes the lsp command to write no response frame to stdout and terminate the process with exit code 1.

An LSP client sending a Content-Length header declaring exactly 16 MiB (16777216) followed by exactly that many bytes of a valid JSON-RPC 'initialize' request body causes the lsp command to write a response frame to stdout containing that request's 'id' and a 'result' object — i.e. the frame is read and dispatched normally, not rejected by the size check.
The lsp command's response to an 'initialize' request advertises capabilities.hoverProvider as false.

An LSP frame whose header block reaches the blank-line terminator without ever supplying a usable Content-Length (header absent, or present but unparsable as an integer) causes the lsp command to write no response frame to stdout and terminate the process with exit code 1.

An LSP input stream that ends (true EOF, zero bytes read at all before the connection closes) causes the lsp command to exit with code 0; no response or error frame is written to stdout as a result of the EOF itself.

An LSP client that sends one or more complete header lines (e.g. 'Content-Length: 10\r\n') but closes the connection before the blank-line terminator is reached is currently treated identically to AC-005's clean zero-byte EOF: the lsp command exits with code 0 and writes no response frame to stdout. (This collapses a truncated header block into the same code path as a clean disconnect — read_content_length returns the same Err(()) for both. See non_goals for the tracked follow-up to distinguish them.)

An LSP client that declares a valid, in-range Content-Length, then closes the connection before delivering that many body bytes, is currently also treated as a clean disconnect: the lsp command exits with code 0 and writes no response frame to stdout (cmd_lsp's read_exact(...).is_err() branch returns Ok(())). See non_goals for the tracked follow-up to distinguish this from AC-005's clean zero-byte EOF.

An LSP client whose header block contains bytes that are not valid UTF-8 (e.g. the raw bytes 'Content-Length: 10\xFF\r\n\r\n') is currently treated identically to AC-005's clean zero-byte EOF: the lsp command exits with code 0 and writes no response frame to stdout, because reader.read_line(...).unwrap_or(0) == 0 maps the resulting io::Error to the same 0-bytes-read outcome as EOF, which read_content_length in turn maps to the same Err(()) as AC-005/AC-005b. See non_goals for the tracked follow-up to distinguish this from AC-005's clean zero-byte EOF.

A frame declaring a valid, in-range Content-Length whose body bytes are not parsable as JSON causes no response frame to be written for that frame; the read loop continues, and a subsequent well-formed initialize frame sent on the same stream still receives a response frame containing that request's 'id' and a 'result' object.

A frame declaring a valid, in-range Content-Length whose body parses as JSON but has no string 'method' member causes no response frame to be written for that frame; the read loop continues, and a subsequent well-formed initialize frame sent on the same stream still receives a response frame containing that request's 'id' and a 'result' object.
